lead.t: The edinger-westphal nucleus of the midbrain is activated by visual stimuli, which sends signals through the oculomotor nerve (cranial nerve III).

snip.t: The edinger-westphal nucleus of the midbrain is activated by visual stimuli, which sends signals through the oculomotor nerve (cranial nerve III).
Posterior communicating or internal carotid artery aneurysm: a third (oculomotor) nerve palsy (ptosis, dilated pupil, "down and out" eye) with retro-orbital pain.
Increased intracranial pressure (ICP) also produces oculomotor nerve palsy because of the presence of temporal lobe compression of the nerve during tentorial herniation.
Uncal herniation compresses the oculomotor nerve → fixed dilated pupil.

qs.q: During the physical examination of a patient with a head injury, which finding is a classic sign of uncal herniation resulting from oculomotor nerve compression?
qs.e: Uncal herniation typically causes an ipsilateral dilated fixed pupil due to compression of the third cranial nerve against the tentorium. This is followed by contralateral hemiparesis and potentially decerebrate posturing.
